html:
"Karakalpaks", Turkic for "black hats", is the map's label, for 1100, for the Black Hoods of the Rus chronicles, Turkic nomads who served the princes of Rus as border guards.

They were groups such as the Torks, Berendei and remnants of the Pechenegs, settled mostly along the Ros river south of Kyiv in the 1100s to guard against the Cumans. They took part in the princes' wars and had a say in who held Kyiv. They were scattered by the Mongols in the 1200s. Whether the modern Karakalpaks near the Aral Sea descend from them is not settled. The map places them farther northeast than the chronicles do.
sum: "Karakalpaks", Turkic for "black hats", is the map's label, for 1100, for the Black Hoods of the Rus chronicles, Turkic nomads who served the princes of Rus as border guards.
